trickyParts: Finding 1 is a behaviour correction to a rule this pull request itself introduced, so its prose in packages/envoy/AGENTS.md and cmd/dispatch/README.md moved with it: reply_to_block is the named item's, and POST /api/v1/comments/{id}/reply always names a block of that comment.

Finding 7 changes an ask's parts hash, so the first reindex of an already-answered ask replaces its answer part. Nothing deployed holds ask parts (migration 0150 is new here), so no live reference moves.

Finding 2 reaches existing data: once 0151's seed is drained, heldByABlock lists a link written in an ask's question from its question part, so a build without the dashboard fix would relabel existing backlinks. That is why the browser row, not a unit test, is its proof.

discoveredComplexity: A reply's reply_to_block is read against the item the request named, never the thread's head: in an ask's thread one block id can name both a block of the comment and a part of the ask, and the two answer differently.

The dashboard, the hover card and the CLI each read a block node as its item, so the item kinds live in one exported set per surface (BLOCK_ITEM_KINDS in the web, ITEM_KINDS in the client) and a fourth kind reaches every reader.
The pull request's contract change census is in the body: four inputs answer differently than on main, with the emitter search and the stored-text statement behind the rollout line.
